text:
sam: Quick design question — the rule list in the policies editor feels visually dense on 1080p. Thoughts on reducing vertical height per rule while keeping drag handles and inline validation visible? Screenshot: https://figma.redwood/example-compact julia: I was thinking compact rows: trim paddings, move secondary metadata into a trailing overflow menu. Keep primary rule name and priority visible. But a11y note — hit targets should stay >=44px. :thinking_face: kevin: Agree. We can visually compress but keep a larger interactive area via CSS (padding hit area vs visual height). Implementation detail: add --rule-row-min-height var so we can tune without layout thrash. maya: Accessibility: when users reorder rules via keyboard or drag, screen readers currently just say 'list updated' which is not helpful. We should announce 'Rule “Allow internal” moved to position 2 of 5'. Proposed aria-live snippet:
Rule 'Allow internal' moved to 2 of 5
oliver: Also, validation states: collapsed rows only show a red dot for conflicts — no text. Can we surface a 1-line message or accessible label like 'Conflicts with higher-priority rule'? Maybe an inline tooltip on hover and an offscreen text for screen readers. julia: For collapsed mode we can show a short label (max ~40 chars). Full explanation in hover or details pane. Copy suggestion: 'Conflicts with higher-priority rule.' Short and actionable. kevin: Dev note: add aria-describedby on the pill that links to an offscreen element id with the message. e.g. aria-describedby="rule-123-conflict" and put Conflicts with higher-priority rule. Keeps visual minimal but readable to AT. maya: Also ensure reorder exposes state programmatically: update aria-posinset/aria-setsize or use aria-live messages, and preserve keyboard focus on the moved item. Use aria-grabbed for drag interactions and announce 'moved up'/'moved down'. sam: On preview simulation: currently we open a modal with results table. Suggest an inline compact simulation toggle per rule list row that can animate which rule matched for sample requests. That would help debugging ordering without losing context. Must respect reduced-motion preference. :eyes: julia: Prototype idea: compact rows + a chevron to expand a small preview panel under a rule that shows sample traffic and which rule matched. Will attach figma frames. cc @kevin for perf constraints. kevin: Feasible but watch very long lists (200+ items). We'll need virtualization and stable DOM ids so announcer mapping isn't lost when items recycle. Also test that aria-live messages map to the current visible label after virtualization. maya: Accessibility copy to standardize: aria-live message template 'Rule {label} moved from position {old} to {new}.' For conflicts: 'Rule {label} conflicts with {higherLabel}.' Please add these to the accessibility checklist and include automated axe checks where possible. oliver: Copy approved. Next steps: @julia update the microcopy and compact-row spec (spacing, hit-target, overflow menu behaviour). @kevin can you sketch the aria attributes we need in a tiny dev spec? If all good I'll block 30m for a sync to finalize visuals and acceptance criteria. julia: Will update and upload the spec in 10 minutes. :sparkles: kevin: I'll draft the small aria snippet and virtualization notes after your upload. maya: I'll prepare the QA checklist and a11y test cases (keyboard reorder, live region readouts, focus management). sam: Awesome — thanks all. Let's keep the compact mode opt-in for now behind a feature flag until we validate on real policies.
